title.blind_remark: left in English, not translated into Estonian

hud.cast.note: Fishing sense of 'õnge viskama' (cast the line); imperative like the guide's buttons.

hud.reel.note: kerima = reel the line in; matches the pass name Autokerimine. 'Tõmba' (pull) is the plainer alternative but has no good pass-name form.

hud.bait_left.note: Label form so 0, 1 and 12 all read correctly (no numeral agreement).

catch.success.note: 'Püüdsid ...' would need the genitive of both inserted words; after a colon rarity and fish stay nominative and agree for every pair. Capitals mid-line read as item tags (guide accepts this for egg.hatched).
catch.success.blind_remark: with the inserted names this reads e.g. "Müütiline Kuldne karpkala", with a capital letter on both words mid-phrase

catch.new_record.note: For the developer: {weight} arrives as 12.4; Estonian writes 12,4 (decimal comma). Fix in the game's number formatting.

fish.golden_carp.note: Follows Minecraft's Estonian 'Kuldne õun' pattern; nominative base form for {fish}.

fish.lantern_eel.note: Coined compound latern + angerjas (lantern eel), keeps the lantern idea. Genitive-stem 'Laternaangerjas' is also correct but the double a reads clumsily.

rarity.mythic.note: Tier above Legendaarne; nominative adjective so it fits before any {fish}.

shop.rods.note: õng = fishing rod (never 'varras', a metal rod).

shop.equip.note: Pairs with the state label Kasutusel; 'Varusta' sounds like supplying gear.

shop.buy_robux.note: Genitive after 'eest' is correct for every price; Robuxi declined without apostrophe per EKI.
shop.buy_robux.decision_reason: Draft was right: the et-ee guide and EKI decline brand names plainly (Robuxi); the dispute came from the keep-term lint rejecting case endings, now fixed.

pass.auto_reel.note: Same verb as hud.reel (Keri); auto- prefix as in 'autosalvestus'. 'Automaatkerimine' (16) is clearer but over the 14 budget.
pass.auto_reel.blind_remark: the "auto-" prefix in Estonian compounds usually means "car", so it can also read as "car reeling"

pass.lucky_bait.note: Õnnesööt built like 'õnnejook' from õnn (luck) + sööt (bait). Restructured to 'doubles the chance to catch rare fish'.

sell.done.note: 'kala' is the same form for 1 and for many; genitive 'mündi eest' is correct for 1 and 340 alike.

ascend.button.note: ülendus = promotion in rank, the prestige sense without religion or climbing; noun label like the guide's 'Taassünd'. 'Tõus' (rise) was rejected: it also means getting up.
ascend.button.blind_remark: a noun ("elevation/exaltation/promotion"), not a verb; uncommon, bookish word for a button

ascend.confirm.text: Kas oled ülenduseks valmis? Alustad otsast peale, kuid püüad haruldasi kalu {bonus}% sagedamini.
ascend.confirm.note: Same Ülendus term as the button. 'Alustad otsast peale' = start over. Percent with no space, per guide.
ascend.confirm.review_reason: "Kas soovid kohe ülendust?" reads like asking for a job promotion rather than confirming an action; "Kas oled ülenduseks valmis?" is the natural game confirm, keeps the Ülendus term, and the dialog itself carries the "now".

weather.storm.text: Torm on tulekul! Haruldased kalad näkkavad.
weather.storm.note: näkkama = the fishing sense of biting (fish taking the bait).

quest.catch_n.note: 'kala' is identical in nominative and partitive, so it reads right for n = 1 and more. Moonlit Bay translated as Kuuvalguse laht (like Tallinna laht), inessive 'lahes'.

quest.claim.note: Guide's claim button; exactly 10 of 10. Never 'Nõua'.
quest.claim.blind_remark: can also read as "Accept", as in accepting a new task, rather than collecting a reward

friends.boost.note: Statement, not an order; partitive 'õnne' after the percent, like the guide's '+{percent}% boonust'.

trade.sent.note: Spoken toast 'You offered {player} a trade'; declined head noun 'mängijale' keeps the name nominative. 'Vahetuspakkumine saadetud mängijale {player}' is 37, over 33.

trade.accept.note: Name as subject in the nominative; no gender in Estonian. 'your trade' left implicit.

codes.redeemed.note: 'Enjoy your reward' rendered as 'the reward is yours'; 'Naudi oma auhinda' reads translated.

afk.kicked.text: Olid liiga kaua tegevuseta ja kalastamine peatus.
afk.kicked.note: Says only that fishing stopped, no removal from the server, as in the source.

event.ends.note: For the developer: {time} arrives as '2d 4h' with English unit letters; Estonian writes '2 p 4 t'. Fix in the game's time formatting.
event.ends.blind_remark: grammatical only if {time} is in the genitive case, e.g. "5 minuti"; a plain number-plus-unit value may read wrong

daily.streak.text: {day}. päev järjest! Tule homme tagasi ja saa veel auhindu!
daily.streak.note: Ordinal '{day}. päev järjest' (day N in a row) avoids numeral agreement and is how Estonian says a streak. 'for more' made explicit as more rewards, per context.

tip.night.text: Vihje: mõned kalad näkkavad ainult öösel.
tip.night.note: 'Vihje:' is the usual tip label; lowercase after the colon; näkkama = fishing bite.

group.join.text: Liitu meie kogukonnaga ja saa 50 sööta tasuta!
group.join.note: kogukond matches Roblox's Community name (guide); 'meie' as in the guide's group reference line.

leaderboard.biggest.note: Heaviest single fish, the usual Estonian fishing-contest category; 'Suurim saak' could read as the biggest total haul.
